questions.question:
The correct decreasing order of energy for the orbitals having, following set of quantum numbers:
(A) n=3,ℓ=0, m=0
(B) n=4,ℓ=0, m=0
(C) n=3,ℓ=1, m=0
(D) n=3,ℓ=2, m=1

[JEE MAINS 2022, 27Jul, Shift-2]
questions.explanation: Option A is correct. First, identify the orbitals from the given quantum numbers: (A) represents 3s, (B) represents 4s, (C) represents 3p, and (D) represents 3d orbital. According to the (n + l) rule, the orbital having greater value of (n + l) possesses higher energy. If two orbitals have the same value of (n + l), then the orbital with higher value of n has higher energy. For 3s, n + l = 3; for 4s, n + l = 4; for 3p, n + l = 4; and for 3d, n + l = 5. Between 4s and 3p, both have equal (n + l) value, but 4s has higher n value, so it has higher energy. Therefore, the decreasing order of energy is 3d > 4s > 3p > 3s, that is, (D) > (B) > (C) > (A).

questions.question:
The angle of elevation of the top \( P \) of a vertical tower \( P Q \) of height 10 from a point \( A \) on the horizontal ground is \( 45^{\circ} \). Let \( R \) be a point on \( A Q \) and from a point \( \mathrm{B} \), vertically above \( R \), the angle of elevation of \( \mathrm{P} \) is \( 60^{\circ} \). If \( \angle B A Q=30^{\circ}, \mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{d} \) and the area of the trapezium \( P Q R B \) is \( \alpha \), then the ordered pair \( (d, \alpha) \) is:

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(Q\) be the foot of the tower and \(PQ=10\).

Since the angle of elevation of \(P\) from \(A\) is \(45^\circ\),

\(\tan45^\circ=\dfrac{PQ}{AQ}\).

Thus

\(1=\dfrac{10}{AQ}\),

so

\(AQ=10\).

Let \(R\) be the point on \(AQ\) vertically below \(B\).

Since \(AB=d\) and \(\angle BAQ=30^\circ\),

\(AR=d\cos30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3d}{2}\)

and

\(BR=d\sin30^\circ=\dfrac d2\).

Therefore,

\(QR=AQ-AR=10-\dfrac{\sqrt3d}{2}\).

From \(B\), the angle of elevation of \(P\) is \(60^\circ\).

The vertical rise from \(B\) to \(P\) is

\(PQ-BR=10-\dfrac d2\).

Hence

\(\tan60^\circ=\dfrac{10-\dfrac d2}{10-\dfrac{\sqrt3d}{2}}\).

Therefore,

\(\sqrt3\left(10-\dfrac{\sqrt3d}{2}\right)=10-\dfrac d2\).

Expanding,

\(10\sqrt3-\dfrac{3d}{2}=10-\dfrac d2\).

Thus

\(d=10(\sqrt3-1)\).

Now

\(BR=\dfrac d2=5(\sqrt3-1)\).

Also,

\(QR=10-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot10(\sqrt3-1)\)

\(=10-5(3-\sqrt3)\)

\(=5(\sqrt3-1)\).

The parallel sides of trapezium \(PQRB\) are \(PQ\) and \(BR\), and the distance between them is \(QR\).

Hence

\(\alpha=\dfrac12(PQ+BR)\cdot QR\)

\(=\dfrac12\left(10+5(\sqrt3-1)\right)5(\sqrt3-1)\)

\(=25\).

Therefore,

\((d,\alpha)=\left(10(\sqrt3-1),25\right)\),

which is option \(A\).

questions.question:
The area of the region enclosed by \( y \leq 4 x^{2}, x^{2} \leq 9 y \) and \( y \leq 4 \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The given region is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis.

So required area is twice the area on the right side of the \(y\)-axis.

For a horizontal strip,

\(x^2\le 9y\Rightarrow x\le 3\sqrt y\)

and \(y\le 4x^2\Rightarrow x\ge \dfrac{\sqrt y}{2}\)

Also \(0\le y\le 4\)

Therefore, required area is

\(\displaystyle 2\int_0^4\left(3\sqrt y-\dfrac{\sqrt y}{2}\right)dy\)

\(\displaystyle =2\int_0^4\dfrac{5\sqrt y}{2}\,dy\)

\(\displaystyle =5\left[\dfrac{2}{3}y^{3/2}\right]_0^4\)

\(\displaystyle =\dfrac{10}{3}\cdot 8\)

\(\displaystyle =\dfrac{80}{3}\)

Consider a curve \( y=y(x) \) in the first quadrant as shown in the figure. Let the area \( A_{1} \) is twice the area \( A_{2} \). Then the normal to the curve perpendicular to the line \( 2 x-12 y=15 \) does NOT pass through the point.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
From the figure, the curve passes through \((4,2)\).

The two shaded areas together form the rectangle of area \(xy\) after removing the rectangle of area \(4\cdot2=8\).

Thus, \(A_1+A_2=xy-8\).

Since \(A_1=2A_2\), \(A_1=\dfrac{2}{3}(xy-8)\).

Also, \(A_1=\displaystyle\int_{4}^{x}y(t)\,dt\).

Therefore, \(\displaystyle\int_{4}^{x}y(t)\,dt=\dfrac{2}{3}(xy-8)\).

Differentiating gives \(y=\dfrac{2}{3}(y+xy')\), so \(y=2xy'\).

Hence \(\dfrac{dy}{y}=\dfrac{dx}{2x}\), giving \(y=C\sqrt x\).

Using \((4,2)\), we get \(C=1\), so the curve is \(y=\sqrt x\).

The given line has slope \(\dfrac{1}{6}\), so a normal perpendicular to it must have slope \(-6\).

For \(y=\sqrt x\), the normal slope is \(-2\sqrt x\), so \(-2\sqrt x=-6\) gives \((x,y)=(9,3)\).

The normal is \(y-3=-6(x-9)\), or \(y=-6x+57\).

It passes through \((6,21)\), \((8,9)\), and \((12,-15)\), but at \(x=10\) it gives \(y=-3\), not \(-4\).

Therefore, it does not pass through \((10,-4)\), so option C is correct.

questions.question:
The equations of the sides \( A B, B C \) and \( C A \) of a triangle \( A B C \) are \( 2 x+y=0, x+p y=39 \) and \( x-y=3 \) respectively and \( P(2,3) \) is its circumcentre. Then which of the following is NOT true?

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The side \(AB\) is \(2x+y=0\), the side \(BC\) is \(x+py=39\), and the side \(CA\) is \(x-y=3\).

The vertex \(A\) is the intersection of \(AB\) and \(CA\).

From \(2x+y=0\), we get \(y=-2x\).

Substituting in \(x-y=3\), we get \(x+2x=3\).

Therefore, \(x=1\) and \(y=-2\), so \(A(1,-2)\).

The circumcentre is \(P(2,3)\), so the square of the circumradius is \(PA^2=(1-2)^2+(-2-3)^2=26\).

The vertex \(B\) is the intersection of \(2x+y=0\) and \(x+py=39\).

Using \(y=-2x\), we get \(x-2px=39\).

Therefore, \(x_B=-\dfrac{39}{2p-1}\) and \(y_B=\dfrac{78}{2p-1}\).

Since \(PB^2=26\), we have \(\left(-\dfrac{39}{2p-1}-2\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{78}{2p-1}-3\right)^2=26\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{(4p+37)^2+(81-6p)^2}{(2p-1)^2}=26\).

Hence \((4p+37)^2+(81-6p)^2=26(2p-1)^2\).

Expanding gives \(16p^2+296p+1369+36p^2-972p+6561=104p^2-104p+26\).

Therefore, \(52p^2+572p-7904=0\).

Dividing by \(52\), we get \(p^2+11p-152=0\).

Factoring gives \((p-8)(p+19)=0\).

Therefore, \(p=8\) or \(p=-19\).

For \(p=-19\), the point \(B\) becomes \((1,-2)\), which is the same as \(A\).

This makes the triangle degenerate, so \(p=-19\) is rejected.

Hence \(p=8\).

Therefore, \(B\left(-\dfrac{13}{5},\dfrac{26}{5}\right)\).

The vertex \(C\) is the intersection of \(x+8y=39\) and \(x-y=3\).

From \(x-y=3\), we get \(x=y+3\).

Substituting in \(x+8y=39\), we get \(9y+3=39\).

Thus \(y=4\) and \(x=7\), so \(C(7,4)\).

Now \(AC^2=(7-1)^2+(4+2)^2=36+36=72\).

Since \(9p=9\cdot 8=72\), statement \(\mathrm{A}\) is true.

Also, \(AC^2+p^2=72+64=136\), so statement \(\mathrm{B}\) is true.

Using \(A(1,-2)\), \(B\left(-\dfrac{13}{5},\dfrac{26}{5}\right)\), and \(C(7,4)\), the area is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{cc}-\frac{18}{5}&\frac{36}{5}\\6&6\end{array}\right|\).

Therefore, the area is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\left|-\dfrac{108}{5}-\dfrac{216}{5}\right|=\dfrac{162}{5}\).

Since \(\dfrac{162}{5}=32+\dfrac{2}{5}\), the inequality \(32<\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)<36\) is true.

But \(34<\dfrac{162}{5}<38\) is false because \(\dfrac{162}{5}<34\).

Therefore, statement \(\mathrm{D}\) is not true.

Hence the correct option is \(\mathrm{D}\).

A circle \( C_{1} \) passes through the origin \( O \) and has diameter 4 on the positive \( x \)-axis. The line \( y=2 x \) gives a chord \( O A \) of circle \( C_{1} \). Let \( C_{2} \) be the circle with \( O A \) as a diameter. If the tangent to \( C_{2} \) at the point \( A \) meets the \( x \)-axis at \( P \) and \( y \)-axis at \( Q \), then \( Q A: A P \) is equal to :

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The circle \(C_1\) has centre \((2,0)\) and radius \(2\).

\((x-2)^2+y^2=4\)

\(\Rightarrow x^2+y^2=4x\)

The chord line is \(y=2x\).

\(\Rightarrow x^2+4x^2=4x\)

\(\Rightarrow x(5x-4)=0\)

The second intersection apart from \(O\) is \(A=\left(\dfrac{4}{5},\dfrac{8}{5}\right)\)

The circle \(C_2\) has \(OA\) as diameter.

Its centre is \(\left(\dfrac{2}{5},\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\)

The slope of the radius joining the centre of \(C_2\) to \(A\) is \(\dfrac{\frac{8}{5}-\frac{4}{5}}{\frac{4}{5}-\frac{2}{5}}=2\)

The slope of the tangent at \(A\) is \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(y-\dfrac{8}{5}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow x+2y=4\)

The tangent meets the axes at \(P=(4,0),\ Q=(0,2)\)

\(QA=\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{8}{5}-2\right)^2}=\dfrac{2\sqrt5}{5}\)

\(AP=\sqrt{\left(4-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^2+\left(0-\dfrac{8}{5}\right)^2}=\dfrac{8\sqrt5}{5}\)

\(\Rightarrow QA:AP=1:4\)

If the length of the latus rectum of a parabola, whose focus is \( (a, a) \) and the tangent at its vertex is  \( x+y=a \), is 16 , then \( |a| \) is equal to:

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]

Let the focal length of the parabola be \(p\).

The length of the latus rectum is \(4p\).

\(4p=16\)

\(\therefore p=4\)

\(\dfrac{|a|}{\sqrt{2}}=4\)

\(\therefore |a|=4\sqrt{2}\)

\(|\overrightarrow{AP}|^2-\dfrac{(\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\vec v)^2}{|\vec v|^2}=24\)

If the line of intersection of the planes \( a x+b y=3 \) and \( a x+b y+c z=0, a>0 \) makes an angle \( 30^{\circ} \) with the plane \( y-z+2=0 \) then the direction cosines of the line are

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The normals of the two planes are \(\vec n_1=(a,b,0)\) and \(\vec n_2=(a,b,c)\).

A direction vector of their line of intersection is

\(\vec d=\vec n_1\times\vec n_2=(bc,-ac,0)\)

\(\Rightarrow \vec d\propto(b,-a,0)\)

The normal of \(y-z+2=0\) is \(\vec n=(0,1,-1)\).

Using the angle between a line and a plane,

\(\sin 30^\circ=\dfrac{|\vec d\cdot\vec n|}{|\vec d||\vec n|}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac12=\dfrac{|a|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\sqrt2}\)

\(\because a>0\), \(|a|=a\)

\(\Rightarrow 2a^2=a^2+b^2\)

\(\Rightarrow b^2=a^2\)

\(\Rightarrow b=\pm a\)

For \(b=a\), the direction cosines may be taken as \(\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt2},-\dfrac1{\sqrt2},0\right)\), which is option \(\mathrm{B}\).

For \(b=-a\), the same calculation gives the line direction \((1,1,0)\), whose direction cosines are \(\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt2},\dfrac1{\sqrt2},0\right)\), which is option \(\mathrm{A}\).

The condition \(a>0\) does not determine the sign of \(b\).

The question is ambiguous as printed, and option \(\mathrm{B}\) is the intended answer only when \(b>0\) is additionally assumed.

questions.question:
A water tank has the shape of a right circular cone with axis vertical and vertex downwards. Its semi-vertical angle is \( \tan ^{-1}(3 / 4) \). Water is poured in it at a constant rate of 6 cubic meter per hour. The rate (in square meter per hour), at which the wet curved surface area of the tank is increasing, when the depth of water in the tank is 4 meters, is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let the depth of water be \(h\) metres and the radius of its upper surface be \(r\) metres.

The semi-vertical angle is \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac34\right)\).

Therefore, \(\tan\theta=\dfrac rh=\dfrac34\).

Hence \(r=\dfrac{3h}{4}\).

The slant height of the water cone is \(l=\sqrt{h^2+r^2}\).

Substituting \(r=\dfrac{3h}{4}\), we get

\(l=\sqrt{h^2+\dfrac{9h^2}{16}}\).

Thus \(l=\sqrt{\dfrac{25h^2}{16}}=\dfrac{5h}{4}\).

The volume of water is \(V=\dfrac13\pi r^2h\).

Therefore, \(V=\dfrac13\pi\left(\dfrac{3h}{4}\right)^2h=\dfrac{3\pi h^3}{16}\).

Differentiate with respect to time.

We get \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{9\pi h^2}{16}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Given \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=6\) and \(h=4\), we obtain

\(6=\dfrac{9\pi(4)^2}{16}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Therefore, \(6=9\pi\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Hence \(\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{2}{3\pi}\,\mathrm{m/h}\).

The wet curved surface area is \(A=\pi rl\).

Substituting \(r=\dfrac{3h}{4}\) and \(l=\dfrac{5h}{4}\), we get

\(A=\dfrac{15\pi h^2}{16}\).

Differentiate with respect to time.

Thus \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{15\pi}{8}h\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

At \(h=4\), we get

\(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{15\pi}{8}(4)\left(\dfrac{2}{3\pi}\right)\).

Simplifying gives \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=5\,\mathrm{m^2/h}\).

Hence the required answer is \(5\).

Let \( f \) be a differentiable function satisfying \( f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} f\left(\frac{\lambda^{2} x}{3}\right) d \lambda, x>0 \) and \( f(1)=\sqrt{3} \) if \( y=f(x) \) passes through the point \( (\alpha, 6) \), then \( \alpha \) is equal to ______.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Put \(\lambda=\sqrt{3}u\) in the given equation.

Then \(f(x)=2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}f(xu^2)du\).

Now put \(t=xu^2\), so \(du=\dfrac{dt}{2\sqrt{xt}}\).

Therefore, \(f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f(t)}{\sqrt{t}}dt\), or \(\sqrt{x}f(x)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f(t)}{\sqrt{t}}dt\).

Differentiating gives \(\dfrac{f(x)}{2\sqrt{x}}+\sqrt{x}f'(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{\sqrt{x}}\).

Thus, \(2xf'(x)=f(x)\), whose solution is \(f(x)=C\sqrt{x}\).

Since \(f(1)=\sqrt{3}\), we get \(C=\sqrt{3}\), so \(f(x)=\sqrt{3x}\).

The point \((\alpha,6)\) lies on the graph, so \(6=\sqrt{3\alpha}\).

Therefore, \(36=3\alpha\), giving \(\alpha=12\).

questions.question:
23−131×7+43−33+23−132×11+63−53+43−33+23−133×15+…+303−293+283−273+…+23−1315×63 is equal to.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
General terms of the given series 

Tn=(2n)3-(2n-1)3+(2n-2)3-(2n-3)3+⋯+23-13n×(4n+3)

\(T_n=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^n\left[(2 k)^3-(2 k-1)^3\right]}{n(4 n+3)}\)

\(T_n=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^n\left[12 k^2-6 k+1\right]}{n(4 n+3)}\)

\(T_n=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^n\left[12\left(\frac{n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}\right)-6\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)+n\right]}{n(4 n+3)}\)

\(T_n=\frac{n^2(4 n+3)}{n(4 n+3)}=n\)

Now \(\sum_{n=1}^{15} T_n=\frac{15 \cdot 16}{2}=15 \times 8=120\)

questions.question:
A common tangent \( T \) to the curves C1:x24+y29=1 and C2:x242-y2143=1 does not pass through the fourth quadrant. If \( T \) touches \( C_{1} \) at \( \left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right) \) and \( C_{2} \) at \( \left(x_{2}, y_{2}\right) \), then \( \left|2 x_{1}+x_{2}\right| \) is equal to.....

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let the common tangent be \(y=mx+c\).

For the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1\),

\(c^2=4m^2+9\)

For the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{42}-\dfrac{y^2}{143}=1\),

\(c^2=42m^2-143\)

Equating the two values of \(c^2\),

\(4m^2+9=42m^2-143\)

\(38m^2=152\)

\(m^2=4\)

\(c^2=4(4)+9=25\)

The tangent that does not enter the fourth quadrant is

\(y=2x+5\)

It can be written as \(2x-y+5=0\).

For the ellipse, the point of contact is

\(x_1=-\dfrac{4(2)}{5}=-\dfrac85\)

\(y_1=-\dfrac{9(-1)}{5}=\dfrac95\)

For the hyperbola, the point of contact is

\(x_2=-\dfrac{42(2)}{5}=-\dfrac{84}{5}\)

\(y_2=\dfrac{143(-1)}{5}=-\dfrac{143}{5}\)

\(|2x_1+x_2|=\left|2\left(-\dfrac85\right)-\dfrac{84}{5}\right|=\left|-\dfrac{100}{5}\right|=20\)

\(\therefore |2x_1+x_2|=20\)

questions.question:
Let \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}\) be three non-coplanar vectors such that \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=4 \vec{c}, \vec{b} \times \vec{c}=9 \vec{a} \) and \(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=\alpha \vec{b}, \alpha>0\). If \(|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|=36\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to_____

 

[JEE Main 2022, 27 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(|\vec a|=A\), \(|\vec b|=B\) and \(|\vec c|=C\).

From \(\vec a\times\vec b=4\vec c\), the vector \(\vec c\) is perpendicular to both \(\vec a\) and \(\vec b\).

From \(\vec b\times\vec c=9\vec a\), the vector \(\vec a\) is perpendicular to both \(\vec b\) and \(\vec c\).

From \(\vec c\times\vec a=\alpha\vec b\), the vector \(\vec b\) is perpendicular to both \(\vec c\) and \(\vec a\).

\(\therefore\) the three vectors are mutually perpendicular.

Taking magnitudes, \(AB=4C\).

Also, \(BC=9A\).

Dividing the second relation by the first relation, \(\dfrac{BC}{AB}=\dfrac{9A}{4C}\).

\(\dfrac{C}{A}=\dfrac{9A}{4C}\)

\(4C^2=9A^2\)

\(C=\dfrac{3A}{2}\)

Using \(AB=4C\), we get \(AB=6A\).

\(B=6\)

The given sum of magnitudes is \(A+B+C=36\).

\(A+6+\dfrac{3A}{2}=36\)

\(\dfrac{5A}{2}=30\)

\(A=12\)

\(C=18\)

From \(\vec c\times\vec a=\alpha\vec b\), we get \(CA=\alpha B\).

\(18\times12=6\alpha\)

\(\alpha=36\)

\(\therefore\) the required value is \(36\)
